newsitem.title: GERMANY: Foreign buyers rule German markets May-July - Buba.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buyers rule German markets May-July - Buba.

text.p: Foreign investors increased their German equity and bond holdings between May and July this year, but domestic banks were cautious bond buyers and sold the share market, the Bundesbank said in its September report.
Foreign buyers invested a net 15.7 billion marks in German shares in the period, counting net sales of two billion marks in July, but domestic banks reduced their shareholdings by 17.6 billion marks.
The Bundesbank attributed foreign interest to the global currency picture and high prices on many foreign stock markets.

International investors also showed "lively interest" in German bonds, increasing their investments more than five-fold to 22.3 billion marks in the period and putting more than half of their funds into the public sector.
However, domestic banks cut their investments in bonds to 17.3 billion marks from 40.7 billion in the previous quarter.
German and foreign issuers raised a total of 58.4 billion marks through fixed income issues in the period versus 51 billion in the previous quarter. Banks accounted for two-thirds of that volume.

"Issuing activity was restrained on the German share market from May to July," the Bundesbank said, noting that the market value of German shares issued in the period had dropped to 3.9 billion marks from 5.2 billion in the previous quarter.
A net 400 million marks in foreign equities were issued, a sharp drop from 5.9 billion marks the previous quarter.
Funds raised from investment fund sales dropped by half to 13 billion marks from 26.2 billion the previous quarter.
